rounds.question: 'Exact action' for file writes: the effect hash today includes the full tool input (the content). Remembering a write by PATH only means a future write of ANY content to that path is pre-approved; by full content it never matches again (you'd be asked every edit). Which?
/permissions already exists as a central chat command that shows and sets the permission MODE. How should learned decisions appear?

How should learned decisions reach a scheduled job? Evaluated live on every job permission request (revocable instantly via Forget) or materialized into the job's own grants when the job is created/updated (stable, but Forget doesn't reach already-materialized jobs)?

The judge-offline notice: 'once per conversation per outage episode' — is process-local best effort enough (today's runtime is a single launchd process), or must it be cluster-durable across runtimes?

In /permissions, a remembered decision can say which scheduled jobs it covers. Show only jobs that have ACTUALLY used it (from the job's permission audit trail) or every job that MIGHT match it in future?

A card that already has a CARDSIMPLE-1 family rule ('Allow for future: all npx vitest commands') would now show two remembering buttons: the new [Allow] plus the family one. How should that card look?

The `file` tool has no capability id: it is on the default tool surface and its list/read address the agent's OWN artifact store, not the filesystem. Does enabling the baseline tool itself satisfy AF-AC2's 'approved capability' clause for silent list/read, or must silent reads wait for a new literal capability id?
In a group chat, when a member taps Allow/No and the host cannot resolve WHO tapped (no acting person id), what should happen?

Batch cards (several permission asks coalesced into one card with Allow all / Review each / Deny all) have no single scope to remember. Should batch cards stay once-only, with remembering available only when you tap 'Review each' and decide the members one by one?

Reading an attachment already in the chat (`attachment_open`): should it skip the card ONLY in auto mode (as a low-risk action the judge path allows), or in every mode including ask and auto_strict (a true birthright in the deterministic rails)?
/permissions shows the 10 newest remembered decisions with Forget buttons. AF-AC8 says you can forget EVERY learned decision. How should older records be reached?

In a group chat the agent's request has no 'memory person' (decision 0118), so even after someone taps Allow, the next identical request has no person's memory to consult and would ask again. What should groups do?
